name: Poland
summary: Descendants, spouse and parents have a money claim for half (two thirds for minors) of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Poland has no trusts but since May 2023 allows family foundations.
reserved_share: Descendants, spouse and parents who would inherit on intestacy: a money claim (zachowek) for half of their intestate share, two thirds for minors or those permanently unable to work (Civil Code art. 991). Lifetime gifts are added back; gifts older than ten years to non-heirs, and contributions to a family foundation after ten years, drop out.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Poland is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. There are no domestic trusts. Family foundations (fundacja rodzinna) have existed since the Act of 26 January 2023 on family foundations, in force 22 May 2023. That Act also amended the reserved-share rules.
open_questions: Art. 991 and the ten-year rule come from law-firm briefings (WKB, Clifford Chance), not the Journal of Laws text.
Tax rules for family foundations and for foreign trusts held by Polish residents were not sourced.
e-Justice Poland page is internally inconsistent (says there are no reserves but describes a reserved-share claim).

sources.title: HCCH status table: Convention of 1 July 1985 on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
